slides.title: Spoken Tutorial on Understanding APIs
slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **Understanding APIs**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,

• Define what an **API** is and its significance.
• Explain the role of an **API** as a connector in **AI** applications.
• Describe how **API** keys ensure secure access and authentication.
• Apply the concept of **API** interaction to send requests and receive **AI**-generated responses.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration: To follow this tutorial, you should have **Python** basics for **API**.

slides.title: What is an API and Why it Matters?
slides.narration:
What is an **API**?
An **API**, or **Application Programming Interface**, is a messenger.
It takes your requests to a system.
Then, it brings the system's response back to you.
**APIs** are crucial for software communication.
They help different programs share data.
Think of it like a universal remote for devices.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing API as a messenger between two systems, with data flowing back and forth.

slides.title: Inputs, Outputs, and Security
slides.narration:
What about inputs, outputs, and security?
**Prompts** are the specific inputs you send.
These go through an **API** to an **AI** model.
A **prompt** tells the model what task to do.
For secure access to these services, we use **API** keys.
**API** keys are credentials for authentication.
They control who can access the system.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a prompt being sent to an AI model via an API, with a key icon representing API keys for secure access.

slides.title: How Applications Interact with AI
slides.narration:
How do applications interact with **AI**?
Applications send structured requests.
These requests contain **prompts** and parameters.
They go to an **AI** model via its **API**.
The model processes your input.
Then, it sends back an **AI**-generated response.
This completes the interaction cycle.
slides.image_prompt: Diagram showing an application sending a request with a prompt to an AI model through an API, and receiving an AI-generated response.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined **APIs** as essential connectors.
We discussed **prompts** as inputs.
We understood **API** keys for security.
And we explored the request-response flow for **AI** interaction.
